test_title: RRB Technician Grade III 2025: Morning Practice Day 2
subject: general
question: In a convex mirror, the principal focus is located _____.

options.text: at the pole of the mirror

solution:
The correct answer is __**behind the mirror**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• In a convex mirror, also known as a diverging mirror, the principal focus is located behind the mirror.
 
• The principal focus is a point from which all the reflected rays appear to diverge after reflecting from the mirror.
 
• Convex mirrors always form virtual, erect, and diminished images, regardless of the position of the object.
 
• The principal focus of a convex mirror is considered to be a virtual focus because the reflected rays do not actually meet at the focus.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Convex Mirror Applications:**

 
 
• Commonly used as rear-view mirrors in vehicles due to their ability to provide a wider field of view.
 
• Employed in security and surveillance systems in stores, hospitals, and other establishments.
 
• Used in road safety to allow drivers to see around bends and intersections.
 
 
 
• **Principal Focus:**
 
 
• The point where parallel rays of light either converge or appear to converge after reflection or refraction.
 
• In convex mirrors, the principal focus is virtual and located behind the mirror.
 
 
 
• **Image Formation:**
 
 
• Convex mirrors always form virtual, erect, and diminished images regardless of the object's position.
 
• These mirrors are useful for providing a wider field of view compared to plane mirrors.
 
 
 
• **Mirror Formula:**
 
 
• The mirror formula relates the object distance (u), image distance (v), and focal length (f) as 1/f = 1/u + 1/v.
 
• For convex mirrors, the focal length (f) is always positive.
